summary.text: Tom Cole is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Oklahoma's 4th District, seeking re-election. A former history instructor and political consultant, he held Republican Party and state government posts in Oklahoma, including state senator and Secretary of State, before his 2002 election to Congress. He chairs the House Appropriations Committee and is an enrolled member of the Chickasaw Nation.

paragraphs.text: Tom Cole was born April 28, 1949, in Shreveport, Louisiana; his official biography describes him as a fifth-generation Oklahoman whose family returned to Oklahoma during his childhood, and says his father served 20 years in the U.S. Air Force.
He holds a B.A. from Grinnell College, an M.A. from Yale University and a Ph.D. from the University of Oklahoma, and was a Thomas Watson Fellow and a Fulbright Fellow at the University of London.
He worked as a college instructor in history and politics, and is a founding partner and past president of CHS & Associates, an Oklahoma City political consulting and survey research firm.
Cole's early political career included stints as district director to U.S. Rep. Mickey Edwards, chairman of the Oklahoma Republican Party, and member of the Oklahoma State Senate.

He served as Oklahoma's Secretary of State under Gov. Frank Keating from 1995 to 1999, including leading the state's effort to secure federal funds for rebuilding after the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing.

On the national party side, he was executive director of the National Republican Congressional Committee in the 1992 cycle, chief of staff of the Republican National Committee in the 2000 cycle, and chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee in the 2008 cycle.
Cole was first elected to the U.S. House in 2002 and has represented Oklahoma's 4th District since 2003.
He has served on the House Appropriations Committee since 2009 and now chairs it; he previously chaired the House Rules Committee and served as a Republican Deputy Whip.

An enrolled member of the Chickasaw Nation, he has been Republican co-chair of the Congressional Native American Caucus since 2009. According to his official biography, he lives in Moore, Oklahoma, with his wife, Ellen.
